sections.title: Sound of the letter
paragraphs: The letter name is (Y) /aɪ/. Its main sound is heard in the word (yes) /jɛs/, which shows agreement. This letter makes four sounds in English.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: First, raise the front of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Keep the air flowing smoothly as your voice hums. For the second sound, spread your lips and make a quick, high sound. For the third sound, open your mouth wide, then glide your tongue up. For the fourth sound, relax your mouth and make a quick, short sound. Touch your throat to feel each sound vibrate.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: At the start of a word before a vowel, it sounds like (yard) /jɑːd/. At the end of an unstressed syllable, it sounds like (happy) /hæ.pi/. In a stressed open syllable or a one-syllable word, it sounds like (cry) /kraɪ/. In a closed syllable inside words of Greek origin, it sounds like (myth) /mɪθ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not add a friction noise when you start the first sound. Keep the air smooth, unlike the sound in jam. At the end of words, do not stretch the vowel into a long sound. Keep it light and quick instead. When it stands alone in small words, make sure your mouth glides completely from open to close.
